scope: Final visible Draft; exact source, article, action-state, and deployed-JSON bytes; generation and publication timing; FleetRunner physical-trial claims, G7 gates, and merge identities; BookcaseDiscovery F-0 execution context, machine-agreement semantics, sampling limits, later-card status, and historical PR dispositions; workstation-yuri #11 scope; current review registry/discovery state; and held action custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: F-0 ran on a local session dataset, not a FleetRunner NAS machine
findings.location: Lines 11 and 48 claim shared NAS infrastructure and call sf-store-001 a physical store machine running the production NAS image.
findings.explanation: The pinned F-0 report identifies sf-store-001 as a 616-frame training-source session and says the evaluation ran on a Mac with a local catalog, offline helpers, and network fetches refused. It did not use the FleetRunner trial adapter, NAS image, or host-local FleetRunner credentials.
findings.correction: Describe sf-store-001 as the video-session dataset and the evaluation as a local Mac run; keep it independent from the FleetRunner NAS physical-trial infrastructure.

findings.title: F-0 was not a reproducibility comparison against a frozen reference run
findings.location: Line 48 equates machine agreement with label-distribution comparison against a frozen reference and treats divergence as nondeterminism or drift.
findings.explanation: The pre-registration defines machine agreement as agreement among the stack's own stages and readers. The report compares aggregate rates on different inputs, video frames versus high-resolution stills, and records expected differences and hypotheses rather than an exact-output replay verdict.
findings.correction: Say the run measures internal stage/reader agreement on the video sample and compares aggregate rates with pilot-000; do not interpret differences as failure, nondeterminism, or environment drift.

findings.title: The source does not establish stride robustness or later-card readiness
findings.location: Line 62 says the metric is robust to the every-three stride, calls F-0 complete as a gate, and clears TS-0 and TS-2 to proceed.
findings.explanation: The source covers one-third of the session, says frames are not independent and provides no confidence intervals, and warns that recurrence at three-second spacing differs from one-second spacing. The report lists the remaining frames, sf-store-002, TS-0, and TS-2 as not done.
findings.correction: Report a bounded one-third-session observation. Do not claim stride robustness or that this sample itself establishes acceptance/readiness for TS-0 or TS-2.

findings.title: Core #590 is not an evidenced G7 prerequisite
findings.location: Lines 86 and 88 and retained candidate 1 say G7 is blocked on deciding whether core #590 must merge first.
findings.explanation: Core #590 is a Proposed SMB tenant-identity ADR and says bookcase backup needs no code change. The source-current #578 checkpoint names transport, SSH, and restore qualification as G7 blockers without making #590 a prerequisite.
findings.correction: Preserve the documented G7 blockers. Treat any relationship between #590 and G7 as unsupported until an owner records that gate; do not claim rerun risk or blocked status from it.

findings.title: Proposed review records are not an unverified backlog and #531 is unrelated
findings.location: Line 94 calls Draft review PRs an unverified audit trail; candidate 2 lists ten PRs, including #531, while calling them nine review PRs.
findings.explanation: The discovery service intentionally exposes eligible open review-only PRs as proposed/current records, and their handoffs identify supervised finding disposition as the next step. Daily-logger #531 is a Selfco telemetry-cutover code PR, not an article review.
findings.correction: Distinguish completed proposed review publication from supervised finding disposition; do not call intentional Draft review records unverified or include unrelated #531 in a review-backlog action.

findings.title: BookcaseDiscovery #37 and #59 do not lack all disposition
findings.location: Line 96 and retained candidate 3 say #37 and #59 have no explicit disposition and tie closing or parking them to G7.
findings.explanation: Core #593 explicitly makes #37 historical context and replaces it with the frozen #95 packet. #37 records its bounded incomplete trial. #59 records a bounded daytime test and is stacked on closed #53. Neither source makes its next decision depend on G7.
findings.correction: Retain #37 as superseded historical evidence. Reconcile #59 against the delivered resident-worker lineage and its closed base as a separate owner decision, without inventing a G7 dependency.

findings.title: workstation-yuri #11 is not merely a prose rename
findings.location: Line 96 calls #11 a prose rename and retained context calls it unblocked with no open gate.
findings.explanation: PR #11 also admits yojimbo in the server device enum and changes HTTP/WebSocket check-in and replay behavior. Its body says service reload and live verification remain separately tracked.
findings.correction: Describe the prose plus server-compatibility slice and retain the separate reload/live-verification gate; do not call it prose-only or fully unblocked.

findings.title: Two displayed commit references are not Git SHAs
findings.location: Lines 25 and 37 display 593-merge and 594-merge as commit references.
findings.explanation: Those strings are not hexadecimal Git object identities. PR #593 and PR #594 have actual landed commit SHAs; #594 is 321a44637b8fc406b8823a192c1194511007e6c0.
findings.correction: Use the actual landed commit SHAs or omit commit bullets when the collector lacks a source-verified identity.

findings.title: Closure of all six physical trials lacks a durable public receipt
findings.location: The title, summary, lines 11 and 86 say the physical loop and G6 are complete with six verified trials.
findings.explanation: Core #593 says its source merge does not claim full G6. BookcaseDiscovery #97 fixes the sixth-trial verifier but says target-machine execution remains required. The source-current #578 checkpoint says lid/Wi-Fi trials remain open, and no later public six-trial packet or checkpoint receipt was found.
findings.correction: Publish the bounded six-trial receipt with source/image pins, unique trial IDs, independent receipt references, fence/sequence evidence, and verdicts before certifying G6 closed; until then mark closure unverified.
